items.title: The truncated first moment of a Gaussian row

source.anchor: Appendix C.2 A3.SS2.p11 / Ex106 and scalar p12 / Ex108–109; row law and cutoff in p1/p10
source.attribution: On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling, arXiv:2610.20492v1.
source.scope: The one-row tail integral and the scalar component of the bias calculation.

items.statement: At the cutoff \(L=2r+3\log(1000d)\), the discarded squared radius has a finite expectation.
assumptions: Let \(d,q\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(2q+1<d\) and put \(r=q+1\). The case \(q=0\) gives \(r=1\).
The unscaled row is \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_r)\) with Euclidean squared norm \(R=\|Z\|^2\). Put \(L=2r+3\log(1000d)\).
The expectation and tail probabilities use the standard Gaussian measure. The level integral uses real Lebesgue volume on \((0,\infty)\), and the separate boundary term uses the tail at zero.
The discarded event is \(R>L\). The retained event \(R\le L\) includes equality. Both integrability conditions in the producer are proved.

obligations.label: The exact strict-tail first-moment identity and bound in Ex106.

bindings.boundary: The exact p11 scalar identity and bound feed the actual scalar bias in p12. The shifted tail is an internal estimate. The shared row-family law, simultaneous truncation event, matrix covariance and concentration, full Fact C.6, Lemma 4.4 and the lower bounds have separate obligations. Public integration, browser acceptance and purification are pending.

assumption_deltas.source: The source row has the standard r-dimensional Gaussian law and the standing range 2q+1<d.
assumption_deltas.lean: The canonical standard Gaussian on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin(q+1)) and the literal source range.
assumption_deltas.reason: The Euclidean row norm and standard variance are fixed.

assumption_deltas.source: The source writes a finite discarded expectation and a finite level integral.
assumption_deltas.lean: The producer also establishes the two integrability facts, with explicit Lebesgue volume on the open ray.
assumption_deltas.reason: The endpoint of the level integral has zero volume and finiteness is a proved conclusion.

assumption_deltas.source: The scalar p12 argument keeps R≤L and discards R>L, then divides the discarded expectation by r.
assumption_deltas.lean: The private application proves the range, exact bias and its upper bound for the actual scalar.
assumption_deltas.reason: The norm mean and the complementary event split are proved inside the module.
